source.section: PIT-ADJ instructions PDF page 7, line 25, Table 2 and Examples 1 and 2; Form PIT-1 lines 9 to 18 and 22; instructions PDF page 25, line 12; Tax Rate Table PDF pages 1 to 6, rows; PDF page 7 (T-7), over 100,000

worked: Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = private pension (person 0) 50,000.00 + taxable Social Security (85% of gross 20,000.00) 17,000.00 = 67,000.00. Federal taxable income = 67,000.00 - standard deduction 15,750.00 - 1 x 1,600.00 additional for age 65 or older = 49,650.00 (federal senior deduction ignored; Form PIT-1 takes only the federal line 12 amount, and no line for what the federal return subtracts after line 12). Form PIT-1, married filing separately. Line 9 federal AGI 67,000.00. Line 10 0.00 (standard deduction taken). Line 11 additions 0.00. Line 12 federal standard deduction 17,350.00. Line 13 dependents 0.00. Line 14 0.00: federal AGI 67,000.00 is over the worksheet's printed ceiling 27,500.00 for this status, so the worksheet is not completed. Line 15, PIT-ADJ: line 13 age 65 or older: Table 1 (married filing separately) row for federal AGI 67,000.00 gives 0.00 x 1 qualifying = 0.00; line 25 Social Security: federal AGI 67,000.00 does not exceed the Table 2 maximum 75,000.00 (married filing separately), so the 17,000.00 included in AGI is exempt = 17,000.00; PIT-ADJ line 28 total 17,000.00. Line 17 = 67,000.00 + 0.00 - 17,350.00 - 0.00 - 17,000.00 = 32,650.00. By the projection: state_agi = federal taxable income 49,650.00 - 17,000.00 = 32,650.00; less base deductions 0.00 gives 32,650.00. Line 18 tax, schedule as numbers: 1.5% x 4,000.00 = 60 + 3.2% x 8,500.00 = 272 + 4.3% x 12,500.00 = 537.5 + 4.7% x 7,650.00 = 359.55; total 1,229.05, to the cent 1,229.05. The table row over 32,600 to 32,700 gives 1,229; expected keeps the formula figure. Lines 19 to 21 0.00. Line 22 net New Mexico income tax 1,229.05.
